Create a standalone Shiny app for the dittoHeatmap module

Source: R/dittoHeatmap_module_app.R
dittoHeatmapApp.Rd

Generates a Shiny application with a selector over the provided objects, a read-only Metadata Preview, and the interactive heatmap with its settings. Needs ComplexHeatmap, InteractiveComplexHeatmap and circlize.

Usage

dittoHeatmapApp(
  object_list = NULL,
  defaults = NULL,
  hide.inputs = NULL,
  hide.tabs = NULL
)

Arguments

object_list

An optional named list of SingleCellExperiment, Seurat, or SummarizedExperiment objects. If NULL (the default), list("example_sce" = example_sce) is used as example data.

defaults

A named list of input IDs and their default values to apply on startup. With the example data, they are applied over the settings the module gallery opens the module on, a key given here replacing its showcase value.

hide.inputs

A character vector of input IDs to hide. Their values are still initialized and used, but the controls are not shown in the UI.

hide.tabs

A character vector of tab names to hide. Inputs in these tabs are still initialized and used. NULL (the default) keeps the module's own default.

Value

A Shiny app object.

Details

When object_list is not provided (or NULL), the app launches with the bundled example_sce dataset.

With the example data, the app opens on the settings the module gallery (sciModuleGalleryApp()) opens this module on.

See also

dittoHeatmapInputsUI(), dittoHeatmapOutputUI(), dittoHeatmapServer(), example_sce

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

library(sciVizModules)
if (requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("InteractiveComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("circlize", quietly = TRUE)) {
    app <- dittoHeatmapApp()
    if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
}
